review.review: The run stopped alive after 128 accepted fallback waits, not death or a frozen clock. The initiating defect is a descent-gate category mismatch: tools/priority_resources.py:15–29 includes food in pickup priorities, while the played tools/mage_policy.py:418–430 treats every priority target as mandatory upgrade/strength progression. Decision 3442, log line 9825, records exactly one target: an unreachable remembered ration at cell 157, with eternal-fire buffers on component boundaries. The upgrade at cell 1543 was picked up at decision 3112; decision 3113 shows its quantity rising from one to two and a public pickup confirmation (lines 8863–8866). The erroneous veto then led to near-full-health healing at decision 3442 and waiting from decision 3443 through 3570 (lines 9827–10212). The final accepted wait advances the clock to turn 3483. Complete log and source browsing resolve the misleading progression diagnosis without reconstructing runtime memory. The proposed focused correction excludes food from this unconditional gate while retaining priority pickup, strict loot refusal, honest unfinished-loot deferral, mandatory upgrades/strength and matching keys. A reduced selector fixture, not a replay or a certified replacement route, produced two expected assertion failures on original policy; all five new tests pass on the candidate. The full Python suite passes 1,540 tests with four skipped. No claim is made that this solves the fire room or proves safe subsequent descent. The separate older unknown-supply preparation issue remains unresolved.
review.learnings: Separate valuable pickup priorities from mandatory progression. Inspect the actual veto targets rather than trusting its upgrade/strength wording. Keep optional hazard-room food unfinished and logged when descent is otherwise admitted; never infer collection, relax fire safety, or guess potion effects. This isolated gate repair does not establish puzzle success or future survival.
